# Controls

<!-- Generated by `membrane checks doc` from controls/checks.yaml. Do not edit by hand. -->

This file lists each membrane check, its evidence, and its control mapping. The mapping is membrane's own. NIST and the SCF Council did not review it.

## Status words

A check gets one status: PASS, FAIL, NO_EVIDENCE, STALE, or INELIGIBLE. A control gets one rollup status: MET, PARTIAL, or NOT MET. MET means every mapped check is PASS. NOT MET means no mapped check is PASS. PARTIAL is the rest. See docs/CONTRACTS.md section 7.

## Evidence rules

- `evidence_kinds` must all have records. Freshness applies to the newest eligible record of each kind.
- `supporting_kinds` join when they exist. An empty supporting kind does not cause NO_EVIDENCE.
- Only `live` records are eligible unless the run passes `--allow-nonlive`. That run is a demonstration.
- A record with `collected_at` after `--now` does not count.

## SCF source

SCF statements below are quotes from the Secure Controls Framework (SCF) 2026.3, sheet "Assessment Objectives 2026.3". Copyright remains with the SCF Council. License: CC BY-ND 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nd/4.0/ . Workbook SHA-256 `5a89bf2d3c106a9a87d4b6e3d62dd3e147d0e960d4c07473045a10aa8a7df697`. The quotes come from Beacon's vendored `rows.json` (SHA-256 `85bd32502899ff908bb55fee3b1c79f56864565702446bb77fbaf10875725162`). Quotes longer than 200 characters are cut and end in "...". The ids are unchanged.

ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A ids are not in this file. The standard text is not public, and membrane does not cite ids that it cannot check against the source.

## OSCAL output

`membrane checks run` writes `assessment-results.oscal.json` (OSCAL 1.1.3). Each check is one observation. Each control is one finding. NIST findings target `<control>_smt` as a `statement-id`. SCF findings target the `ao_id` as an `objective-id`. MET maps to `satisfied`. PARTIAL and NOT MET map to `not-satisfied`. The prop `membrane-control-status` keeps the membrane word. `import-ap` points at `./assessment-plan.placeholder.json`. That file does not exist. Replace the href with the real assessment plan before you use the document in a package.

## Checks

### AGT-INV-01 No unregistered agent workloads

- Question: Does every running agent workload have an entry in the agent registry?
- Target: Zero workloads carry a membrane.io/agent-id label with an id that is not in the registry. Zero workloads in an agent namespace have no membrane.io/agent-id label. Membrane infrastructure workloads carry the label membrane.io/component and are exempt. The newest inventory record of each cluster is the population.
- Evidence kinds: inventory
- Supporting kinds: none
- Max age: 24 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Register each listed workload with a manifest in registry/agents, or remove the workload from the cluster.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CM-8, CM-8(3)

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AAT-07.1_A02 | AAT-07.1 | "the organization tracks AI models and AI agents deployed in production environments, capturing: (1) ownership; (2) intended purpose; and (3) status." |
| AST-09_A04 | AST-09 | "discovered Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) are compared against existing inventories to identify assets not present in the inventory." |

### AGT-INV-02 No manifest drift on running agents

- Question: Does each running agent carry the manifest hash that the registry holds for it?
- Target: Zero registered agent workloads have a membrane.io/manifest-sha256 annotation that is missing or that differs from the registry hash of that agent.
- Evidence kinds: inventory
- Supporting kinds: none
- Max age: 24 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Redeploy the listed workload from the current registered manifest through the pipeline, or roll back the out-of-band change.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CM-2, CM-3

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CFG-08.2_A07 | CFG-08.2 | "unauthorized deviations from an approved secure baseline configuration are identified by automated mechanisms." |
| AAT-07.1_A03 | AAT-07.1 | "the organization tracks updates to AI models and AI agents, capturing: (1) ownership; (2) intended purpose; and (3) status." |

### AGT-IAM-01 No model-provider credentials outside the vault

- Question: Are all model-provider credentials that the scanner found stored in the vault only?
- Target: The newest secret scan has zero findings with in_vault false.
- Evidence kinds: secret_scan
- Supporting kinds: none
- Max age: 24 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Revoke the listed credential at the provider, issue a new one into the vault, and remove the copy from the listed location.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: IA-5, IA-5(7)

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IAC-14.3_A01 | IAC-14.3 | "unencrypted static authenticators are not embedded in applications or other forms of static storage." |
| CFG-17.2_A04 | CFG-17.2 | "software artifacts are scanned to identify plain text or encoded secrets and keys." |

### AGT-IAM-02 One identity per agent

- Question: Does each agent run under a service account and SPIFFE id that no other agent uses?
- Target: Zero service accounts (namespace and name) and zero SPIFFE ids are used by more than one distinct agent id in the newest inventory of each cluster.
- Evidence kinds: inventory
- Supporting kinds: none
- Max age: 24 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Give each listed agent its own service account and SPIFFE id, and update the manifest runtime block to match.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: IA-4, IA-9

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IAC-36_A02 | IAC-36 | "system services and applications are uniquely identified and authenticated before establishing communications with devices, users or other services or applications." |
| AAT-39.19_A01 | AAT-39.19 | "all AI agent-initiated actions are mapped to authenticated user or system identities, with enforced authorization checks." |

### AGT-AU-01 Every tool execution has an allow decision

- Question: Does every tool execution trace back to an allow decision from the gateway?
- Target: Zero tool_exec records in the window have a decision_id with no matching decision record, a matching decision that is not allow, or a matching decision for another agent, tool, or action hash. A decision_id that more than one tool_exec record names is also a finding.
- Evidence kinds: tool_exec
- Supporting kinds: decision
- Max age: 24 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Route the listed tool backend through the gateway so that it runs only after an allow decision, and investigate each listed execution.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: AU-2, AU-12, AC-3

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AAT-39.3_A03 | AAT-39.3 | "all tool and API invocations by AI agents are subject to access controls." |
| AAT-40.1_A01 | AAT-40.1 | "event logs are generated for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) actions." |

### AGT-AC-01 Irreversible actions have a bound approval

- Question: Does every executed irreversible action have a human approval bound to the same action hash?
- Target: Zero irreversible tool_exec records in the window lack an approval record with the same approval_id and the same action_sha256 that did not expire before the execution time. The registry manifest decides irreversibility for the agent and tool. An unknown agent or tool, or a missing flag, counts as irreversible. A tool_exec irreversible flag that differs from the manifest is also a finding. An approval_id that more than one tool_exec record names is also a finding.
- Evidence kinds: tool_exec
- Supporting kinds: approval
- Max age: 24 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Block irreversible tools in the gateway until a verified approval token for the exact action hash is present, and review each listed execution with its owner.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: AC-3, AC-3(2)

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AAT-36.12_A01 | AAT-36.12 | "human review is performed for high-risk or ambiguous Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT) actions." |
| AAT-36.12_A02 | AAT-36.12 | "clear escalation paths for approval exist for instances involving high-risk or ambiguous AAT actions." |
| AAT-39_A03 | AAT-39 | "AI agents are deployed to securely operate under human oversight." |

### AGT-AC-02 Delegator present where the manifest requires one

- Question: Does every allow decision name a human delegator when the agent manifest requires one?
- Target: Zero allow decisions in the window have an empty delegator for an agent whose manifest sets delegation.requires_delegator true.
- Evidence kinds: decision
- Supporting kinds: none
- Max age: 24 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Fix the authorization policy so that it denies calls with no delegator for these agents, and fix the caller so that it sends the delegator.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: AC-3, IA-2

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IAC-32_A03 | IAC-32 | "processes acting on behalf of users are associated with uniquely identified and authenticated system users." |
| AAT-39.19_A01 | AAT-39.19 | "all AI agent-initiated actions are mapped to authenticated user or system identities, with enforced authorization checks." |

### AGT-SC-01 Egress stays inside the manifest list

- Question: Do agents reach only the destinations that their manifest egress list names?
- Target: Zero allowed flows in the window go from an agent to a destination FQDN that is not in the egress list of that agent manifest. A flow from an unregistered agent id is also a finding.
- Evidence kinds: egress_flow
- Supporting kinds: none
- Max age: 24 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Regenerate the egress network policy from the manifest and apply it, then investigate the listed flows.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: SC-7, SC-7(5), AC-4

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AAT-39.2_A02 | AAT-39.2 | "limitations are implemented for AI agents according to least functionality, where the AI agent is restricted to communicate with the minimal Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) a..." |
| AAT-39.11_A02 | AAT-39.11 | "a "sandbox" capability restricts AI agents from unrestricted access to remote resources (e.g., Internet-based DAAS)." |
| NET-04_A03 | NET-04 | "approved authorizations are enforced for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems based on organization-defined information flow control policies." |

### AGT-CM-01 Deploys pass every gate

- Question: Did every agent deploy in the window pass every pipeline gate and meet the manifest eval threshold?
- Target: Zero deployed pipeline runs in the window have manifest_policy other than pass, aibom other than present, or signature other than verified. When the manifest defines evals, the evals gate result is pass and the score is at or above the manifest min_pass.
- Evidence kinds: pipeline_run
- Supporting kinds: none
- Max age: 720 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Make the listed gate blocking in the pipeline, then rerun the deploy so that every gate runs and passes.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CM-3, CM-3(2), SA-11

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |

### AGT-TST-01 Canary probes pass daily

- Question: Did a canary run in the last 24 hours and did every probe pass?
- Target: The newest canary record is at most 24 hours old, all_pass is true, and every probe has pass true.
- Evidence kinds: canary
- Supporting kinds: none
- Max age: 24 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Fix the policy or gateway path that let the listed probe through, then rerun the canary.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: CA-7, SI-6

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AAT-39.14_A01 | AAT-39.14 | "adversarial testing that simulates attacks against AI agents to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities is conducted per an organization-defined frequency." |
| CPL-07_A06 | CPL-07 | "cybersecurity / data privacy controls are monitored on an ongoing basis to ensure the continued effectiveness of those controls." |

### AGT-IR-01 Kill drill inside 90 days and inside SLA

- Question: Did a kill drill run in the last 90 days and did full denial occur within the SLA?
- Target: The newest kill drill record is at most 90 days old, within_sla is true, and seconds_to_denial is at or below sla_seconds.
- Evidence kinds: kill_drill
- Supporting kinds: none
- Max age: 2160 hours
- Remediation on FAIL: Find the slow step in the kill path, fix it, and run the kill drill again.
- NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5: IR-3, IR-4

| SCF ao_id | SCF control | SCF statement (quote) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AAT-39.13_A01 | AAT-39.13 | "authorized users or operators have the ability to immediately halt or disable AI agent activity in case of unexpected behavior or harm." |
| IRO-09_A04 | IRO-09 | "the effectiveness of the incident response capability is tested per an organization-defined frequency." |
